content.text:
We need to decide how to resolve the March order from Moat Cailin (region id "moat-cailin") with unit IDs 6 and 37 (both Greyjoy knights). ActionGuidance gives reachable regions: greywater-watch, seagard, the-twins, white-harbor, winterfell. For each, triggersCombat flag: only winterfell triggers combat (has Stark units). Others are controlled by Greyjoy or neutral.

We must consider supply constraints: Greyjoy supply = 3 (from observation). Supply track 3 => permitted army sizes: 3,2,2,2 (four armies max; sizes as per table). Currently Greyjoy units: let's list.

Greyjoy units: 
- pyke? Not listed but likely has units at pyke? The board shows pyke controlPowerToken null, garrison 2 (castle), no units listed (maybe there are units but not in board view? Since units list maybe omitted if none). Pyke likely has a ship? Actually we have a ship at port-of-pyke (unit id 7). That is a ship in port, not a land unit. Also knights at moat-cailin (ids 6,37). A footman at greywater-watch (id 9). No other units listed for Greyjoy.

So current armies:
- Knights at moat-cailin: they are together = army size 2 (both in same area => an army). That's a land army counted toward supply.
- footman at greywater-watch: single unit, not an army.
- ship at port-of-pyke: ship unit in a port (port counts as sea area? Ship in port considered land? It's a ship but in port area (sea? Actually port is a special land/sea hybrid but ships are placed there). For supply: ship units in a port are considered part of a sea army? It counts as a sea area army (ships in same sea area make army). Since only one ship, that's not an army (needs >=2). So not counting.

Thus we have one army size 2. Supply allows up to 4 armies with sizes 3,2,2,2. So we have capacity to have 3 more armies, each up to size 2 (or 3 for one). So moving knights elsewhere will likely be okay.

We have the option to leave a control token (power token) when vacating moat-cailin. The actionGuidance says canLeavePowerToken true. If we vacate (remove both knights) and leave control token, we must pay one power token (available 8). That would preserve control of moat-cailin (which currently has no control token -- controller null). Moat-cailin currently has no controlPowerToken (null). If we leave it empty and place a power token, we would gain control of that area (important for supply icons? Moat Cailin has no supply/crown). Not vital maybe but could be useful for future movement.

We need to consider if we want to attack winterfell. Winterfell is controlled by Stark (has garrison 2, unit footman). Combat would involve attacking with knights (strength 2 each) plus March order -0 (since order is March +0). So attacker initial strength = Knights (2 each = 4) + March 0 = 4. Defender has garrison 2 plus footman (strength 1) = 3? Actually footman strength 1 plus garrison 2 = 3. Support around Winterfell? Adjacent areas with support orders: According to revealedOrders, Winterfell has Defense +1 order (which is not support). Support orders adjacent? Let's check adjacent areas to Winterfell: From map: Winterfell neighbours: bay-of-ice, castle-black, karhold, moat-cailin, port-of-winterfell, the-shivering-sea, the-stony-shore, white-harbor. Among these, which have Support orders? castle-black has Support +0 (revealed). karhold has Support +0. moat-cailin is our source with March order, not support. port-of-winterfell none. the-shivering-sea no order. the-stony-shore none. white-harbor none. So there are support orders in castle-black (Stark) and karhold (Stark). These are controlled by Stark, not us, but they can support either side if they choose. Since they are owned by Stark, they could support defending Stark, or choose to support us (Greyjoy) if Stark wants to betray? Usually they would support themselves. For analysis, we assume Stark will support defender (makes sense). However support is optional. So assume they will support defender.

Thus defender support could add combat strength from those areas: castle-black has 2 knights (Stark) => strength 4; karhold has 1 knight => strength 2. Ports? Not support. So defender could get up to 6 additional. That would make defender total 9 (3+6). Attacker 4. Attacker loses.

But could Stark refuse support? Possibly but likely support. Even if they refuse, defender still has garrison2 + footman1 =3. Attacker 4 would win tie? Not tie; they'd win. But we can't rely on them refusing. So attacking Winterfell is risky.

Alternative destinations: greywater-watch (own area, unit present), seagard (own area, no units currently), the-twins (neutral area maybe no controller), white-harbor (neutral), all non-combat. Moving knights into own area consolidates army maybe merges with footman? greywater-watch already has footman. If we move both knights to greywater-watch, we would have an army of 3 units (1 footman, 2 knights). That's army size 3, which is allowed as one of the permitted sizes (3). That's still fine supply.

If we move to seagard (currently empty) we would create an army of size 2 there. Also fine.

If we move to the-twins (no controller) we would create new army size 2; also we could later control area by placing power token if vacated.

If we move to white-harbor (no controller) similar.

Goal: expand control, maybe aim for castles. Which of these have castles? Greywater-watch is a land with a castle? map indicates greywater-watch has "supply=1". Not castle. seagard has no castle. the-twins has crown=1 but not castle. white-harbor has castle=1 (yes white-harbor has castle=1). Let's confirm: white-harbor line: "white-harbor [land; castle=1]: moat-cailin, port-of-white-harbor, the-narrow-sea, the-shivering-sea, widows-watch, winterfell". Yes it has a castle. So capturing white-harbor would give us a castle region (increase victory points). However white-harbor is adjacent to moat-cailin, and currently has no units and no control token. If we move knights there, we would occupy white-harbor with knights, taking control (since we have units). It has a castle, good. No combat because no enemy units. We would gain a castle (increase controlledCastleAreas). That seems beneficial.

Supply wise, moving both knights there creates an army size 2 with castle. Fine.

We need to consider leaving moat-cailin empty. If we move both knights out, we could leave control token to retain control but we have no power token waste? We have 8 tokens, can afford 1. Might be strategic to keep moat-cailin under control for future movement (maybe to support). However we also could later move ships from port-of-pyke through moat-cailin? Not directly. Port-of-pyke is a port connected to pyke (sea). Moat Cailin is land; not a port. So not needed.

Goal: get more castles, increase victory points. White-harbor is a castle, currently uncontrolled. Taking it seems best.

Thus moves: move both knights (ids 6 and 37) from Moat Cailin to White Harbor.

We need to ensure supply: after move, our armies: knights at white-harbor (size2), footman at greywater-watch (size1 alone), ship at port-of-pyke (size1). So still only one army size2, okay.

We will vacate Moat Cailin; we could choose to leave power token. If we do, we spend 1 power token, reducing available to 7. Is there benefit? Moat Cailin currently has no supply/crown, but might be useful later as transport crossing? It is adjacent to the-twins, white-harbor, etc. Could be used as staging area for later moves maybe. Controlling it gives us a land area (counts toward land areas). We already have 5 land areas; adding control token would keep it controlled even without units. Might be beneficial for future expansion. However we might want to preserve power tokens for bids later. Currently we have 8, decent. Might choose not to leave token, but then Moat Cailin becomes unoccupied and unclaimed; control may revert to none (since no power token and no units). The controller would become none, which is okay.

Which is more strategic? Holding Moat Cailin could give us adjacency to white-harbor later for ship transport? Not relevant. Might help to later move units through the-twins? Not essential.

I think we should leave a power token to keep Moat Cailin under control (increase land areas). The cost 1 token is fine.

Thus action: starting_region_id: "moat-cailin", moves list with one entry: destination_region_id "white-harbor", unit_ids [6,37]. leave_power_token: true.

Confirm reachable list includes white-harbor, yes.

Need to ensure that leaving power token is allowed: canLeavePowerToken true. So we set leave_power_token true.

Now produce JSON: {"starting_region_id":"moat-cailin","moves":[{"destination_region_id":"white-harbor","unit_ids":[6,37]}],"leave_power_token":true}

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

leave_power_token.description: Spend one available power token to preserve control when legally vacating the source area. This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established.
leave_power_token.title: Leave Power Token

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
